company: Tallybird is a fictional AI meeting notetaker for teams, sold with a product-led motion: a 14-day Team trial with no credit card, then Pro, Team, Business, or Free. Shared recaps bring in new workspaces.

messages.subject: Activation dip
messages.body: Activation dipped on the weekly dashboard. What is going on, and what do you need from me?

messages.subject: Calendar tickets
messages.body: More new users stuck on the calendar step this week. Several mention needing admin approval.

release.title: Onboarding v2: connect calendar first
release.notes: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

payload.headline: activation_rate_7d fell materially (-7.33% relative, p=5e-6), concentrated in calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces (-22.25%, p=0.0), coinciding with rel_0412's mandatory calendar-connect-first onboarding change.

cause.does_not_prove: That this release caused the activation drop by itself; timing alone is not causation.

evidence.quote: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

cause.text: Release rel_0412, shipped 2026-02-10, changed onboarding so new users must connect their calendar before anything else, and removed the skip option.

cause.does_not_prove: That calendar_provider=microsoft is causally distinct from other explanations; it only shows where the change concentrates.
cause.text: activation_rate_7d for calendar_provider=microsoft fell from 0.3937 to 0.3061 (-22.25% relative, p_value 0.0) between baseline and recent periods, while google (p_value 0.838747) and none (p_value 0.281091) did not move significantly.

cause.does_not_prove: That the first-meeting drop is caused specifically by the calendar-first flow rather than some other change on the meeting-recording path.
cause.text: For calendar_provider=microsoft, calendar_connect_rate_1d rose from 0.3321 to 0.5315 (+60.04%, p=0.0), moving opposite to activation, while first_meeting_rate_7d fell from 0.5248 to 0.4469 (-14.84%, p=0.0), the same direction as the activation decline, making it the earliest funnel step consistent with the drop.

cause.does_not_prove: The full scope of affected workspaces - 21 tickets is a lower bound; most blocked workspaces likely never file a ticket.

evidence.quote: Getting "admin consent required" when I connect Outlook. Our IT team takes a week to approve new apps. Any workaround so I can use the trial meanwhile?
Connect Outlook fails with an admin approval message. A colleague signed up last month and says she didn't have to do this step. Did something change?

cause.text: 21 distinct Microsoft-calendar workspaces filed tickets between 2026-02-12 and 2026-03-01 describing being blocked in onboarding by an Outlook 'admin consent required' error with no way to skip past it.

payload.cheapest_test: Gate rel_0412's removal of the skip option behind a flag scoped to calendar_provider=microsoft (restore the skip option or add a fallback path for Outlook admin-consent-blocked users), then compare first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d for that segment over the next 1-2 weeks against the pre-rel_0412 baseline.
payload.question: Did 7-day activation change in the last few weeks, and if so why?
payload.recommendation: Roll back or flag-gate rel_0412's removal of the skip option for calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces so users hitting the Outlook 'admin consent required' wall can proceed to record a meeting without waiting on IT admin approval, while leaving the calendar-first flow in place for google and none, where it shows no significant harm.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That channel or company_size play no role at all - s51_plus shows a larger-than-average drop - but neither dimension shows the concentrated, near-zero-p_value break that calendar_provider=microsoft does.
ruled_out.text: Channel and company_size splits show broad, roughly uniform declines across nearly all their values (channel: direct -7.19%, organic -7.48%, paid_search -8.17%, recap_link -7.71%; company_size: s11_50 -6.64%, s2_10 -7.28%, s51_plus -15.46%, solo -5.96%), not a single standout segment the way calendar_provider=microsoft is a standout (-22.25%, p=0.0).

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Total number of Microsoft-calendar workspaces silently blocked without filing a ticket - the 21 tickets are a lower bound on scope.
Whether workspaces that eventually get IT admin approval go on to activate normally, or whether the delay itself causes lasting drop-off.
would_change_if: If first_meeting_rate_7d for microsoft recovers to baseline without any onboarding change (e.g., as IT admins approve the app over following weeks), that would suggest a temporary lag rather than a structural block, lowering urgency for rollback.

If reverting the skip removal for microsoft-only does not raise first_meeting_rate_7d back toward baseline within 1-2 weeks, that would suggest the admin-consent wall is not the actual mechanism and another cause should be sought.

findings.claim: The ruled_out section states channel/company_size show broad uniform declines 'not a single standout segment the way calendar_provider=microsoft is a standout (-22.25%, p=0.0)' as if that number is evidenced by this finding.
findings.evidence: review.check_entry numbers check: '22.25' in that text is not in its evidence array (which only cites q_9732131dfcbb and q_8cdc348a1919, the channel/company_size queries, not the microsoft query q_48b8a02dc5de).
findings.impact: A code check failure blocks SHIP outright and, more importantly, a reader can't verify the comparison number cited to justify ruling out channel/company_size without tracing back to a different finding's evidence.
findings.proof_required: Re-run review.check_entry after the edit and confirm numbers: pass.
findings.smallest_action: Add q_48b8a02dc5de to this finding's evidence list (it's already cited correctly in the cause section), or drop the parenthetical and just say 'unlike the concentrated break seen in calendar_provider=microsoft above.'

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the skip for Microsoft calendar workspaces brings their activation back to baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: Microsoft first_meeting_rate_7d not back to its week 1 to 5 level for cohorts after the rollback

builds.message: Add calendar_connect_skip_microsoft flag (off by default) to restore the skip option on the calendar-connect step for calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces, per pkt_0001 / bet_0001. Users on other calendar providers are unaffected; when the flag is off, behavior is identical to today for everyone.
builds.diff:
--- a/tallybird/flags.yaml
+++ b/tallybird/flags.yaml
@@ -11,3 +11,9 @@
   rules:
     - {plan: [business, enterprise]}
   description: The notetaker joins Microsoft Teams calls through the new bot. Beta for Business and Enterprise.
+
+calendar_connect_skip_microsoft:
+  enabled: false
+  rules:
+    - {calendar_provider: [microsoft]}
+  description: Restores the skip option on the calendar-connect step for calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces, so users blocked by Outlook admin-consent approval can proceed to record a meeting instead of being stuck. Rollback of rel_0412's skip removal, scoped to microsoft per pkt_0001.
--- a/tallybird/onboarding.py
+++ b/tallybird/onboarding.py
@@ -21,9 +21,11 @@
 
 def steps(user: dict, flags: Flags) -> list[Step]:
     """The steps for this user, in order. `user` carries calendar_provider (google or microsoft) and plan."""
+    calendar_connect_skippable = flags.is_on("calendar_connect_skip_microsoft", user)
     return [
         Step("calendar_connect", "Connect your calendar",
-             "Tallybird joins the meetings on your calendar and writes the notes for you."),
+             "Tallybird joins the meetings on your calendar and writes the notes for you.",
+             skippable=calendar_connect_skippable),
         Step("welcome", "Welcome to Tallybird", "Here is what a recap looks like."),
         Step("first_meeting", "Record your first meeting", "Start a meeting, or paste a meeting link."),
     ]
--- a/tests/test_calendar_connect_skip_microsoft.py
+++ b/tests/test_calendar_connect_skip_microsoft.py
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+from tallybird.flags import Flags
+from tallybird.onboarding import steps
+from tallybird.screens import render_step
+
+MICROSOFT_USER = {"calendar_provider": "microsoft", "plan": "pro"}
+GOOGLE_USER = {"calendar_provider": "google", "plan": "pro"}
+
+
+def test_flag_off_by_default_microsoft_still_cannot_skip():
+    flags = Flags.load()
+    first = steps(MICROSOFT_USER, flags)[0]
+    assert first.id == "calendar_connect" and not first.skippable
+
+
+def test_flag_on_lets_microsoft_users_skip_calendar_connect():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"calendar_connect_skip_microsoft": True})
+    first = steps(MICROSOFT_USER, flags)[0]
+    assert first.skippable
+    assert 'data-action="skip"' in render_step(first)
+
+
+def test_flag_on_does_not_affect_google_users():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"calendar_connect_skip_microsoft": True})
+    first = steps(GOOGLE_USER, flags)[0]
+    assert not first.skippable
+    assert 'data-action="skip"' not in render_step(first)
+
+
+def test_other_steps_unaffected_by_the_flag():
+    flags = Flags.load(overrides={"calendar_connect_skip_microsoft": True})
+    rest = steps(MICROSOFT_USER, flags)[1:]
+    assert [s.skippable for s in rest] == [False, False]

payload.does_not_prove: That the effect will last, or that the action was the only change in the period.
payload.method: Mature cohorts 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-15 (1433 workspaces) against 2026-02-09 to 2026-03-01. Two-proportion test, p = 0.0.

payload.rationale: The rollback recovered Microsoft activation. Next, retest v2 behind a flag with a consent fallback.

trace.event: Comms is not built yet. Nothing is sent.

cause.mechanism: Onboarding v2 made calendar connect mandatory. About 45% of Microsoft calendar workspaces need admin consent, so they get stuck.

affected.funnel_step: calendar connect step -> first real meeting. Connect completion rises (everyone must try), while consent failures now block the first meeting

cause.secondary_effect: Fewer activations mean fewer shared recaps, so recap_link signups start dipping 1 to 3 weeks later.

findings.finding: Localizes the drop to Microsoft calendar workspaces, not to Teams as a meeting platform.
Names admin consent on the mandatory calendar step as the mechanism.
Cites tickets from 3 or more workspaces.
Computes activation on mature cohorts only (7 full days).
Bonus: sizes the cost in revenue, or flags the delayed viral-loop effect.

correct: Restore the skip option for Microsoft calendar workspaces (or roll back v2 for them), then retest v2 behind a flag with a fallback when consent is required.
Roll back v2 for everyone, then retest behind a flag with the fallback.
partial: Roll back without a retest plan.
wrong: No action by the end of week 8.
Blame the Teams bot, channel mix, or seasonality.

traps: Cohorts from the last 7 days are immature.
Microsoft calendar users skew toward Teams, so a meeting-platform slice points at Teams.
Support tags are noisy: only half of consent tickets are tagged integration.
